lawyer:
AJ Mohammad Ali with Zainul Abedin, with AM Mahbub Uddin, with Bodruddoza Badol, and Md Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate ----- For the Anti-Corruption Commission.
parties:
Begum Khaleda Zia ----- Accused-Petitioner 
Vs 
State ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This application under section 10(3) of the Criminal Law Amendment, 1958 has been filed by the accused-petitioner before this Court for transfer of Metropolitan Special Case No. 177 of 2009, corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 102 of 2008, arising out of Ramna PS Case No. 08 dated 3-7-2008, under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with sections 409/109 of the Penal Code, now pending, before the Court of learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka, to the Court of another Special Judge, Dhaka having jurisdiction to try the case. The prosecution case, as it appears from the application, is that the accused-petitioner Begum Khaleda Zia, during her tenure in the office as Prime Minister during 1991-1996, opened an account in Sonali Bank, Ramna Corporate Branch Dhaka being Account No. 5416 in the name Prime Minister's orphanage fund and a foreign remittance was received in the said account by United Saudi Commercial Bank's DD No. 153367970, dated 9-6-1991 amounting to US$ 12,55,000 equivalent to BDT 4,44,81,216 and that the said money was not utilized during 9-6-1999 to 5-9-1993 but subsequently, a sum of Taka 2,33,33,500 from the received: amount was transferred to Zia Orphanage Trust fund and a sum of Taka 2,33,33,500 was transferred to Zia Memorial Trust. It is alleged that Zia Orphanage Trust had been set up for misappropriation of money for the personal benefit of the accused-petitioner and others. Hence, the FIR was lodged under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 2. However, after lodging of the FIR, the Anti-Corruption-Commission having satisfied with the materials found during investigation into the case submitted charge-sheet against the accused-petitioner and others. The learned Judge of the trial court having received the record of the case from the cognizance Court framed charge and recorded evidence of 32 prosecution witnesses. The prosecution case at present is at the stage for examining the accused-petitioner and others under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 3. It may be noted that on the facts and reasons of apprehension of bias of the learned trial Judge against the accused-petitioner, an application for transfer of the case was made in the Hon'ble High Court Division being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8704 of 2017 and on a contested hearing, a Division Bench of this Court passed an order on 8-3-2017 allowing the transfer of the case to the Court of learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka from, the court of Metropolitan Special Court No. 3, Dhaka. 

 4. It may be further mentioned that, after the order, the learned Judge of the Court of Senior Special Judge, Dhaka took over the Charge of trial of the aforesaid criminal case and the accused-petitioner also entered appearance before the learned Court and the learned Judge of the trial Court fixed the case for recording of the statement of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 13-4-2017. 

 5. It may be stated that on 13-4-2017, an application was filed before the trial Court for referring the instant case to the Hon’ble Supreme Court, High Court Division for transfer of the case from the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka to any other Court of Special Judge alleging, inter-alia, that Mr Md Kamrul Hossain Mollah, the learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka before assuming charge of the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka earlier held an office in the capacity of Director General (DG) of Anti-Corruption-Commission (ACC) from 2010 to 2015 and held such position in charge of legal and prosecution cell of the Anti-Corruption-Commission where he had to examine all criminal case files and litigation matters and for this reasons, it transpires that he had occasion to deal with the prosecution matters with the prosecution team of the Anti-Corruption-Commission regarding all cases including the instant case and further that the learned Judge had dealt with the matters relating to this case from October 2010 to March 2015. 

 6. It is disclosed in the application that the learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka on hearing of the submissions made on behalf of the accused-petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, rejected the application on 13-4-2017 and fixed the case on 27-4-2017 for filing order of the Hon'ble High Court Division failing which examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure would be taken up. 

 8. At the very outset, Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, submits that Mr Md Kamrul Hossain Mollah, the presiding Judge acting as Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka had been involved in dealing with prosecution matters in Zia Charitable case and Zia Orphanage Trust case before assuming charge in 2015 as Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka. He next submits that the learned Senior Special Judge, Dhaka has rejected the application for referring this instant case to the Hon'ble High Court Division, without due and proper application of judicial mind and in rejecting the application, has not denied his involvement acting as Director-General of Anti-Corruption-Commission dealing with the prosecution matters of the instant case against the accused-petitioner Begum Khaleda Zia, and, as such, for ends of justice, this instant case needs to be transferred from the Court of Metropolitan, Senior Special Judge, Dhaka to any other Court of Special Judge, Dhaka. He then submits that the petitioner has reasonable grounds and reasons to apprehend that the defence will not get fair, transparent and proper justice from Mr Md Kamrul Hossain Mollah, the learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka and that he will not be free from bias having once acted and dealt with the prosecution matters against the accused-petitioner holding office as Director General of Anti-Corruption-Commission from 2010 to 2015 till assuming office as Metropolitan Sessions Judge and Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka and considering the above aspects of the case, the present case requires to be transferred to another Court for ends of justice. Learned advocate for the accused-petitioner, in support of his submissions, has referred to a number of decisions in the cases of Manak Lai, Advocate vs Dr Prem Chand reported in AIR 1957 425, Lalita Rajya Lakshmi vs State of Bihar reported in AIR 1957 PATNA 198, Shohali Thakur vs State reported in 19 BLD 103 = 4 BLC 69, RV Bow Street Metropolitan Stipendiary Magistrate and others, ex parte Pinochet Ugarte (No. 2), reported in All England Law Reports (1999) 577. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption-Commission, submits that there is no materials or evidence on record to show that the learned Judge of Special Court has any interest in the subject patter of the case or he has showed any bias towards the accused-petitioner, and, as such, the allegation of bias brought against the learned Judge of the trial Court appears to be somewhat conjectured and surmised. He next submits that the holding of post as Director-General of the Anti-Corruption Commission is legally permitted and approved by section 33 of the Anti- Corruption-Commission Act, 2004. He then submits that the accused-petitioner has brought this application before this Court to gain time only to drag the case for an indefinite time with a view to causing delay in disposal of the case. He lastly submits that the accused-petitioner earlier moved an application for transfer of the case which was allowed by the High Court Division transferring the same and now the petitioner has come before this Court with similar type of application before this Court in order to make a further delay to dispose of the case and the accused-petitioner instead of filing leave to appeal before the Appellate Division, has come before this Court with fresh cause of action with a tactics to make the case delay in disposing of the case, and, as such, considering the above aspects of the case, the application filed by the accused-petitioner may be summarily rejected. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocates appeared for the respective parties. We have also gone through the application for transfer and the supplementary affidavit along with the materials annexed thereto. During hearing of the application for transfer, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission, has produced a letter under Memo No. দুদক/আইন/৪৮/২০৯ (ক্রিঃমিস কেস 14890 dated 7-5-2017 issued by the Assistant Director of (legal and prosecution), Anti-Corruption-Commission, Head Office, Dhaka in order to show that Mr Md Kamrul Hossain Mollah, the learned Judge of the trial Court joined the Anti-Corruption Commission as Director-General on 8-11-2010 and he performed his functions as Director-General there till 19-3-2015 but the FIR of the instant case was lodged on 3-8-2008 and Anti-Corruption Commission submitted charge-sheet on 5-8-2009, and, as such, it appears that the learned Judge of the trial Court had no occasion to deal with accused- petitioner's case. It is evident from the aforesaid letter that Mr Md Kamrul Hossain Mollah, Metropolitan Sessions Judge Dhaka held the office as Director General (legal and prosecution) of Anti-Corruption Commission from 8-11-2010 to 19-3-2015. There is no dispute about the holding of the post as Director-General by the learned Judge stated above. It is true that there is no concrete piece of material or evidence on record to show that the learned Judge mentioned above dealt with the matters relating to Zia Charitable case and Zia Orphanage Trust case, or that he showed any bias against the accused-petitioner. It is obvious that the learned Judge of the trial Court having held the post of Director-General had overseen and supervised so many legal matters produced before him for his legal opinions. 

 11. Eventually, the facts and circumstances of the case demonstrate that the learned Judge of the trial Court was the Director-General of legal and prosecution cell of the Anti-Corruption Commission from 8-11-2010 to 19-3-2015. For this reasons, it has become a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the accused-petitioner that she may not have a fair, impartial and proper justice from the Court as the learned Judge mentioned above was closely associated with Anti-Corruption Commission holding the post of Director-General. Because of the aforesaid reason, the learned Judge of the trial Court may have some interest and weakness towards the Anti-Corruption Commission, which may cause a serious disaster to the rights of the accused-petitioner. It is of the essence of judicial decisions, and judicial administration that judges should be able to act impartially, objectively and without any bias. The legal maxim "memo debet esse judex in causa propria sua" has outlined the principle that a justice who is interested in the subject matter of a dispute should be precluded from acting as Judge therein. This principle applies not only to justices but to all judges, Tribunals and Courts which are given jurisdiction to determine judicially the rights of the parties. There is another maxim governing the field in the matter of dispensation of justice and that another legal adage goes to say that justice should not be done only it should also manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done also. If the allegation of bias attributed to the learned Judge of the trial Court is not removed, the said apprehension of bias rooted in the mind of the accused-petitioner from getting fair justice from a particular Court will click her mind negatively forever. 

 12. On taking consideration of the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates for the respective parties as well as the facts and the attending circumstances of the case and the propositions of law mentioned above, we are of the view that in order to ensure fair justice and remove apprehension of bias created in the mind of the accused-petitioner from getting fair justice from that particular Court, the case is required to be transferred to any other competent Court having jurisdiction to try the same. 

 13. Hence, we are inclined to allow the prayer of the accused-petitioner without issuing any Rule in order to avoid further delay in disposal of the case, as we have heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties at length and in details. 

 14. It appears from the record of the case that the learned Judge of the trial Court in the meantime recorded the evidence of 32 witnesses and the case is awaiting examination for the accused-petitioner and others under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Apart from this, as per submission of the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, the accused-petitioner requires some time to examine safai witnesses in support of her defence case. 

 15. Accordingly, we feel it appropriate to pass necessary order fixing time-limit for disposal of the case as expeditiously as possible. 

 17. Consequently, Special Case No. 3 of 2010 corresponding to Metropolitan Special Case No. 177 of 2009, corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 102 of 2008 arising out of Ramna PS Case No. 8 dated 3-7-2008 under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with sections 409/109 of the Penal Code pending before the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka, be transferred to the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka. 

 18. The learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka is directed to transmit the case record to the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka, at once. The learned Special Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka, is directed to proceed with the case in accordance with law and to conclude the trial within the period of 60 (sixty) days from the date of receipt of this order without giving unnecessary adjournments to the parties concerned herewith.
